ideas.pitch: A mobile web calculator that helps teams instantly compute the optimal truss member lengths and angles for a given bridge span using finite element approximations.
ideas.problem_statement: Build a bridge that carries the most load for the least weight within a 2.5 hour structural design challenge.
ideas.title: TrussPro: Rapid Structural Optimization for Bridge Weight-to-Load
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages finite element analysis principles similar to Tesseract Hackathon winning projects, giving teams a mathematical edge during the 2.5-hour build time instead of guessing.

ideas.pitch: An ultrasonic sensor and microcontroller setup placed underneath the bridge test gap to monitor structural deflection and sound warning frequencies before catastrophic failure.
ideas.problem_statement: Build a bridge that carries the most load for the least weight, evaluated by loading each bridge until failure.
ideas.title: LoadScan: Real-time Bridge Deflection and Failure Predictor
ideas.why_it_could_win: Integrates physical hardware and sensors into a structural challenge, mirroring the hardware-focused winning patterns from ICHack and TechnoMorph.

ideas.pitch: A lightweight offline progressive web app for rapid entry of bridge dry weight and final load-test results to calculate the official score instantly.
ideas.problem_statement: The bridge with the best load-to-mass ratio wins based on weight and maximum load held before failure.
ideas.title: BridgeLab: Instant Mass-to-Strength Scorecard App
ideas.why_it_could_win: Provides immediate utility for event participants and judges to transparently track the leaderboard without manual spreadsheet errors.

ideas.pitch: A quick-sketch browser tool where you draw your bridge profile and visualize simulated weak points under central vertical loads.
ideas.problem_statement: The design is entirely up to you: truss, arch, beam, anything, as long as it spans the test gap.
ideas.title: StressHeat: FEA Stress Visualization Simulator for Paper Bridges
ideas.why_it_could_win: Uses differentiable programming and structural simulation techniques reminiscent of top-tier hackathon winners to demonstrate engineering rigor.

ideas.pitch: A physical LED countdown and phase-alert device tailored specifically for the 2.5-hour build window to keep teams on schedule.
ideas.problem_statement: Every team gets the same kit, the same 2.5 hours and one job: build a bridge that carries the most load for the least weight.
ideas.title: Fallout-Timer: On-Site 2.5-Hour Build Pace Synchronizer
ideas.why_it_could_win: Features custom hardware construction using timing circuits, matching the practical hardware execution seen in winning entries like the washing machine timer circuit.
